scenario.label: Framework SSR · three shared workloads
scenario.boundary: Production HTTP request, routing, SSR and framework response serialization to complete uncompressed HTML over loopback. Static fixture input is available locally; no database or external I/O. Full-document caching is disabled.
scenario.parity: Same semantic business content for 4 sections, 32 cards and 160 feature items; 96 products and 480 SVG stars; and 1,000 rows with 12 cells, formatting, branches, escaping and variable-length tag lists. Every URL carries a request-specific freshness value. Generated wrappers/classes and framework scripts outside the business root may differ. Complete response bytes are retained and checked on every timed request.
limitations: Different framework shells and hydration protocols produce different payload sizes.
This workload does not measure browser hydration, application startup, database I/O or developer experience.
A separate contract and capture from the synchronous pure-renderer suite; numbers must not be combined.

Equal-load rates are fixed per workload (10/5/1 requests per second), identical across frameworks. These rates avoid forcing the largest workload into overload; raw latency sample counts are retained.

Capacity windows are 10 seconds for cards/products and 60 seconds for the table, identical across frameworks. The longer table window captures repeated completion batches from the slowest adapter. Equal-load latency windows are 10 seconds; low-rate tail percentiles have few samples.
